title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. On the previous page Grothendieck has a 'smooth group' object D*_12, read as Γ̂*_12 in the transcription. It is presumably a group-scheme or 'smooth group' model over a base S_0 of the units of Ẑ, or of the ring at level 12, built over the additive group D_1 = G_a. Its group of connected components is the constant group (Z/12Z)* = {±1, ±5}. He chooses a set-theoretic section of D*_12 → (Z/12Z)*_{S_0} using idempotent 'sign coordinates' ν_2, ν_3, which are sections of the constant scheme {0,1}_{S_0}, so ν_p^2 = ν_p. The signs are ε_2 = (-1)^{ν_2} = 1-2ν_2 and ε_3 = (-1)^{ν_3} = 1-2ν_3. The section is μ_0 = (-5)^{ν_2} 5^{ν_3}. Because the ν's are idempotent, 5^{ν_3} = 1+4ν_3 and (-5)^{ν_2} = 1-6ν_2. Hence μ_0 = 1+4ν_3-6ν_2-24ν_2ν_3.

This page.
- A general section is μ = μ_0 + 12[ν_0] = 1+4ν_3-6ν_2+12(ν_0-2ν_2ν_3), with ν_0 a section of G_a.
- He then rewrites μ in 'mod 4 form', (86): μ = ε_2 + 4ν'.
- He rewrites it in 'mod 6 form', (87): μ = ε_3 + 6ν''.
- He checks the compatibility 2ν'-ν_2 = 3ν''-ν_3, both sides equal to 2ν_3-3ν_2-6ν_2ν_3+6ν_0.
- The Proposition summarises. On D*_12 one has functions ν_2, ν_3 (values in {0,1}_{S_0}), ν', ν'' (values in D_1) and μ (values in D_1* ⊂ D_1). μ is the image under D*_N → D*_1; (-1)^{ν_2} is the image in (Z/4Z)*_{S_0}; (-1)^{ν_3} is the image in (Z/6Z)*_{S_0}. Then (89): μ = (-5)^{ν_2}(5)^{ν_3} + 12ν_0 for a uniquely determined section ν_0 of D_1 = G_a.

Purpose. This is an explicit coordinate description of the level-12 unit group as a fibre product. It combines the level-4 data (ε_2, ν') and the level-6 data (ε_3, ν''), glued along the common quantity ν = 2ν'-ν_2 = 3ν''-ν_3, a Chinese-remainder-type gluing over the overlap at 2. The next page records this as (90)–(93), noting that μ = 1 iff ν_2 = ν_3 = ν_0 = 0.

Why this matters in context. In the Longue Marche continuation this most likely serves the analysis of the modular group at level 12 (SL_2(Z) / Γ(12) structures, the 2-3 'Teichmüller' bookkeeping). It amounts to an explicit parametrisation of the unit group (Z/12)* lifted to a smooth group.
errors: (86) and (87) are inconsistent with the expression for μ just above and with (89). Expanding gives 1+4ν_3-6ν_2-12ν_2ν_3+12ν_0, whereas μ_0 contains -24ν_2ν_3. Check with ν_2 = ν_3 = 1, ν_0 = 0: μ = (-5)(5) = -25, but (86)/(87) give -13. With ν_0 as defined in (89), the correct values are ν' = ν_3-ν_2-6ν_2ν_3+3ν_0 and ν'' = ν_3-ν_2-4ν_2ν_3+2ν_0.

Grothendieck's ν', ν'' are correct if ν_0 is replaced by ν_0 - ν_2ν_3, i.e. using the alternative section μ_0' = 1+4ν_3-6ν_2-12ν_2ν_3. That is still a valid lift: -13 ≡ 11 mod 12. So the error is a harmless bookkeeping shift of ν_0, but it is carried into (90) on the next page.
The compatibility relation 2ν'-ν_2 = 3ν''-ν_3 holds with either convention, so the structural conclusion (91) is unaffected.

ideas.what: Lifting (Z/12Z)* = (Z/4)* ×_{(Z/2)*} (Z/6)*-type sign data to explicit sections via idempotent coordinates, e.g. 5^{ν} = 1+4ν, (-5)^{ν} = 1-6ν
ideas.modern_name: explicit section of a smooth group model of units with component group (Z/N)*; Chinese remainder / fibre product decomposition

ideas.what: Description of the level-12 object as glued from level-4 and level-6 data along ν = 2ν'-ν_2 = 3ν''-ν_3
ideas.modern_name: fibre product of congruence-level structures (level lcm(4,6) = 12 from levels 4 and 6)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine explicit coordinate bookkeeping for units mod 12 lifted to a smooth group, with a minor arithmetic slip in the ν_2ν_3 coefficient. No new result or connection is visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line '2ν'-ν_2 = 4ν_3 - ...' should read 2ν_3 (2ν'-ν_2 = 2ν_3-3ν_2-6ν_2ν_3+6ν_0), which matches the second line.
In (86), the symbol between ν_2 and 3ν_2ν_3 is blotted in the image; it is likely an overwritten sign or coefficient. The next page confirms '-3ν_2ν_3'.
The objects are written as a double-struck D (D_12*, D_1*, D_N*), as on the previous page's transcription, rather than Γ̂.
